tasks.short: Write down where each customer file and each chase stands.

today.trigger: A payment, a reminder, a call, or a customer mail changes what the officer believes about an account, several times a day.
steps: Open the debtor in AFAS Profit and read the open items.
Check Outlook for the latest mail and any promise the customer made.
Check the Rabobank line when the customer says the invoice was paid.
Type a note with the status, the date, the contact, and the next action.
Update the Excel list that drives the day's calls.
drudgery: Retyping a promise or a dispute reason that is already in the mail.
Copying the same status into AFAS and into Excel.
Reconstructing the last action when the dossier note is thin.
today.time_sinks: Most of the 153 hours goes on finding the last trace and typing it again, because the ledger, the mailbox, and the call list do not share one status.

lenses.faster: Payment posted, reminder sent, and mail received already carry the status, so the retyping into AFAS and Excel drops away and only an unclear note still needs the officer.
lenses.autonomous: Each posted payment, sent reminder, and inbound debtor mail updates the stage, the promise date, and the last action without a reminder to maintain the sheet.
lenses.ambitious: Every open item, including the small ones that get a note only when someone chases them, would carry a reason code and a next action, which is what makes a cash forecast the sites can trust.
lenses.joy: Copying Outlook into AFAS and Excel is the part that can go. Judging a messy damage or detention dispute is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: For an ambiguous mail, five readings with a reason code and the supporting line: promised, short-paid, disputed, paid-but-unmatched, and wrong debtor.
lenses.altitude: The officer sets the stage list, the reason codes, and the promise rules with the controller, and reviews the exception queue.
reach: The AR bookkeepers' notes on why a payment was left unmatched.
The controller's dispute ageing, which is rebuilt in Excel at month close.
A clean status feed for the FP&A cash-in line.

tasks.human_edge: The officer can hear when a promise is real and when 'it is paid' is a stall, and knows which shipper's AP contact actually decides.
tasks.pattern_why: Payments and reminders follow rules already in AFAS. The open part is turning a mail or a call note into a promise date, a dispute reason, and a next action that can be checked against the open items.

in_practice.trigger: A payment posts, a reminder goes out, a mail arrives on the collections mailbox, or the working day ends.
steps: Read new payments, reminders, and debtor mail since the last run.
Fill promise date, dispute reason, contact, and next action from the mail and the ledger.
Set the collection stage from the agreed rule table.
Write the high-confidence lines onto the AFAS debtor dossier.
Park conflicting and low-confidence lines for the officer.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer confirms a low-confidence line, and any note that sets a dispute or a legal flag, before it is saved.
data_needed: Open items with due date, terms, and remaining amount.
Reminder history and the collections mailbox.
The reason-code list the controller has agreed.
Yesterday's matched Rabobank lines.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS debtor dossier and a collections action log the controller can sample at close.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores debtor open items, dossier notes, and dunning history, and imports bank statements for matching.
Onguard keeps a collections worklist with debtor status and dunning steps for Dutch finance teams.
A model can lift a promise date and a dispute reason from a Dutch email into fixed fields, with a person confirming unclear text.

risks: A wrong promise date flows into the FP&A cash forecast and the close.
Contact names and call notes are personal data under the AVG and need a purpose and a retention period.
Two sources can disagree: the customer says paid, and the bank line is still unmatched.
research_questions: What share of status notes only repeat a payment, a reminder, or a sentence already in Outlook?
Can an AFAS workflow or UpdateConnector write a dossier note and a stage without a customisation project?
How often do the customer's words and the bank line disagree in a typical week?
Will the controller accept machine-written dossier notes in an audit sample?

tasks.short: Find the overdue customers and decide who gets worked today.

today.trigger: The officer starts the day, and again after the bank lines land, by looking for what is past due.
steps: Export open customer items from AFAS to Excel.
Filter on due date and sort by amount and age.
Take off items already promised or marked disputed.
Compare the list with the Power BI ageing from the nightly extract.
Build the day's call and mail list by hand.
drudgery: Rebuilding the ageing in Excel each morning.
Reconciling the live ledger with a dashboard that is one night old.
Scrolling past small items to find the balances that matter.
today.time_sinks: The export, the filters, and the doubt about whether a customer paid yesterday consume the 142 hours, before any call is made.

lenses.faster: The morning export and the manual removal of promised and disputed items disappear, because those flags already sit on the AFAS open item.
lenses.autonomous: After the morning bank import, a queue is built from live open items, grouped by customer, with the rule that put each item on the list.
lenses.ambitious: Every debtor would be watched every day, including small balances, and the queue would produce a weekly cash-in figure the FP&A analysts can put in the forecast.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the ageing in Excel is the part that can go. Spotting a good customer that is quietly slipping is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Three orders for the same queue: by amount, by age, and by a broken promise, so the officer can choose the day's sequence.
lenses.altitude: The officer maintains the rules for terms, grace days, dispute holds, and strategic accounts, and reviews the hits each week with the controller.
reach: The AR bookkeepers' unallocated-cash list, which uses the same open items.
The controller's monthly DSO bridge.
The FP&A weekly cash forecast.

tasks.human_edge: The officer knows which overdue invoice is a proof-of-delivery or tariff dispute that operations already owns, and which shipper pays on a fixed cycle after the due date.
tasks.pattern_why: Overdue is a due date, an open amount, a term, and a status flag. AFAS already holds them, and the queue can be checked against the ledger without a model.

in_practice.trigger: The Rabobank statement has been imported and the morning open-item position is available in AFAS.
steps: Read open items, terms, dispute flags, and promise dates from AFAS.
Apply the house rules for grace days, promises, disputes, and strategic accounts.
Group the remainder by customer with amount, age, and last action.
Rank broken promises and large balances at the top of the day's queue.
Publish the queue for the officer on the finance dashboard.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer chooses the day's calls and any credit hold. Building the queue needs no separate approval.
data_needed: Live open items, not only the nightly extract.
Payment terms and dispute flags on the debtor or the item.
Promise dates and strategic-account flags.
The morning bank-match result.
in_practice.logs_to: The day's queue, stored so the controller can see what was overdue and what was worked.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit produces debtor ageing and open-item lists from due date and remaining amount.
Onguard builds a daily collections worklist from overdue items, disputes, and follow-up status.
A nightly Power BI extract of AFAS will miss payments posted the same morning, so a reliable queue has to read the ledger after the bank import.

risks: A queue on the nightly extract will chase customers who paid yesterday.
A credit hold fired from a stale rule can stop loading at Rotterdam, Tilburg, or Venlo.
Terms that live only in a SharePoint contract will mis-age every invoice for that customer.
research_questions: Are payment terms stored on the AFAS debtor, or only in the contract PDF on SharePoint?
What share of overdue items are disputed proof-of-delivery, detention, or tariff differences?
Does the Rabobank match finish before the officer starts, or only after a bookkeeper clears the statement?
Which accounts has the finance director marked as never to be chased automatically?

tasks.short: Remind overdue customers by mail or phone and ask them to pay.

today.trigger: A customer on the day's list is past the house grace, or a promise date has been missed.
steps: Take the next customer and gather the open invoices from AFAS.
Find the billing contact in the dossier or in old mail.
Send a reminder from a Word or Outlook template, or call.
Write down what was sent or said and when to try again.
For a few large shippers, check with sales before making contact.
drudgery: Assembling the invoice list and the attachments for a standard reminder.
Looking up the right contact and the language for that customer.
Logging the send so the next reminder does not go too soon.
today.time_sinks: The 130 hours sit mainly in preparation and in calls. Personal visits are rare; contact is mail and phone, with an occasional meeting when sales asks.

lenses.faster: The standard reminder, with the right invoices and the right language, goes out from the policy, and the call starts from a one-page brief.
lenses.autonomous: When an item crosses the agreed day count and is not disputed or flagged, the template reminder sends and logs itself. A broken promise or a balance above the threshold waits for the officer.
lenses.ambitious: Every delinquent account would get a timely notice that matches the contract and, where it applies, the statutory collection-cost rules, so a later incasso file is already in order.
lenses.joy: Mail-merge and hunting for the invoice PDF can go. A call that actually settles a dispute is the work worth keeping.
lenses.options: For a sensitive account, three drafts: a short Dutch reminder, an English statement of account, and a call script with the open items.
lenses.altitude: The officer writes the reminder policy with the controller: timing, amounts, language, cost line, and which customers sales may block.
reach: The AR bookkeepers' requests for a statement of account.
The file an external incassobureau asks the controller to assemble.
A first-pass reply to sales when they ask whether a shipper may book.

tasks.human_edge: The phone call, the decision to wait a few days for a long-standing shipper, and the judgment to involve sales before a hard reminder goes to a key account.
tasks.pattern_why: A reminder can start a legal clock and can damage a shipping relationship. The standard steps are repeatable, and a person releases anything outside the policy and makes the calls.

in_practice.trigger: An item crosses a step in the reminder policy, or a promise date passes with the item still open.
steps: Select accounts that crossed the step and are not disputed or flagged by sales.
Fill the reminder in the debtor's language with the open items and the cost line the policy allows.
Send the reminders that sit inside the pre-agreed rule and log them on the debtor.
Prepare a one-page brief for every account that needs a call.
The officer calls, then the outcome and the next date are written back to the dossier.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer agrees the rule in advance, releases any account sales has flagged, and makes every call. A disputed account stays out of the automatic batch.
data_needed: The approved timing, thresholds, and cost line.
Billing contact and language on the debtor.
Sales flags for do-not-auto-mail.
Open items, prior reminders, and dispute status.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS dossier and the sent-items folder of the collections mailbox.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit sends debtor reminders from open items with house layouts and logs the dunning step.
Onguard runs multi-step dunning by mail and records the follow-up on the debtor.
Dutch statutory collection costs and the 14-day notice apply to consumers, and they apply to a business debtor when the contract does not set another rule.

risks: A reminder on a disputed damage claim angers a key account and reaches sales afterwards.
A cost line that the contract does not allow, or that breaches the statutory scale for a sole trader, creates a complaint and an uncollectable extra.
The wrong contact receives invoice detail, which is both a commercial problem and an AVG problem.
A reminder during a customer's known payment run creates noise and trains them to ignore the next one.
research_questions: What share of contacts are a template reminder, and what share are a phone call?
Are the billing contact and the language stored on the AFAS debtor?
Which customers has sales marked as do-not-auto-mail, and where is that flag kept?
For sole traders, does the company apply the statutory collection-cost scale, and is that written on the SharePoint contract template?

tasks.short: Answer customers who have a problem with an invoice or a payment.

today.trigger: A customer mails or calls because they want a copy, a statement, a payment confirmation, or an explanation of a charge.
steps: Read the customer's mail or take the call.
Look up the invoice, the payments, and the open balance in AFAS.
Ask a bookkeeper or a site when the proof of delivery or the rate is unclear.
Write the reply in Outlook and attach the invoice PDF.
File the correspondence on the debtor.
drudgery: Searching AFAS for the invoice PDF and the payment line.
Retyping the open balance into the reply.
Forwarding threads to a bookkeeper for a fact the ledger already holds.
today.time_sinks: The lookup and the drafting of routine replies take most of the 126 hours. Real disputes wait while copies and 'have you received our payment' mails are answered.

lenses.faster: The invoice, the payment, and the open balance are already in the draft reply, so the officer stops searching the ledger for a copy or a status.
lenses.autonomous: A collections mailbox answers a request for an invoice copy, a statement, or a payment status from the AFAS record and files the reply. A dispute, a complaint, or a figure the ledger does not support stays in the queue.
lenses.ambitious: Every customer would get a correct statement the same day, and the company would see which lanes generate the questions: detention, fuel surcharge, damage, address errors.
lenses.joy: Hunting for the PDF and retyping the balance can go. Untangling a real billing argument is the work worth keeping.
lenses.options: When the ledger is ambiguous, two drafts: payment received and not yet allocated, or short-paid against named invoices, each with the supporting lines.
lenses.altitude: The officer defines which question types may be answered from the ledger alone, reviews a weekly sample, and retires templates that cause a second mail.
reach: The AR bookkeepers' 'please resend the invoice' mail.
A clean list of missing proofs of delivery for the sites.
Fewer interruptions for the controller during the close.

tasks.human_edge: An angry customer with a cargo-damage claim needs a person who can own the next step. The ledger cannot decide a commercial credit or admit a liability.
tasks.pattern_why: The reply uses the ledger and the mailbox and goes out under the company's name. Lookup answers are checkable against AFAS. A complaint or a mismatch still needs the officer before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: A mail arrives on the collections address, or a call note is filed, asking about an invoice, a payment, or a balance.
steps: Classify the question as a copy, a statement, a payment status, a dispute, or a complaint.
Pull the invoice, the payments, and the open items from AFAS.
Draft the reply with those figures and attach the invoice PDF.
Send the reply when it is a copy, a statement, or a payment status and the figures match the ledger.
Leave disputes, complaints, and unmatched payments in the officer's queue.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer sees every dispute, every complaint, and any draft the ledger does not fully support. Routine lookup replies send under that rule.
data_needed: The invoice PDF and the open-item position from AFAS, same day.
Matched Rabobank lines for that debtor.
The allowed contact for that debtor.
A question-type list agreed with the controller.
in_practice.logs_to: The collections mailbox and the AFAS debtor dossier.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds the invoice, the open item, and the allocated payment that a status reply needs.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can draft an Outlook reply from the mail thread and attached context.
A customer-facing bot must be identifiable as such, and the company remains responsible for the content of the answer.

risks: A reply from the nightly extract confirms a payment that is not yet in the ledger, or misses one posted this morning.
Invoice detail sent to the wrong person breaches confidentiality and the AVG.
A helpful draft can admit liability on a cargo claim before the claims process has run.
If a bot answers, the customer has to be able to tell, and a person has to be reachable when the answer is wrong.
research_questions: What share of inbound mail is a copy, a statement, or a payment status, and what share is a real dispute?
Can AFAS attach the invoice PDF to an outbound mail with the connectors the company already uses?
Who may receive a customer's open items: the contact on file, sales, or a site planner?
How often is the true answer blocked because the bookkeeper has not yet allocated the bank line?

tasks.short: Convince customers to pay, agree a plan, or settle a damage claim.

today.trigger: A reminder has not been paid, a promise was broken, a direct debit was reversed, or a damage invoice is sitting open.
steps: Call the customer with the open balance and the earlier promises.
Hear the cash problem, the dispute, or the damage claim.
Ask for payment in full or propose a short plan.
Mail a recap of what was agreed.
Tell the controller when a long plan or a write-off is needed.
drudgery: Rebuilding the balance and the promise history on paper before the call.
Writing the recap mail from scratch after the call.
Chasing the controller later because the plan was never written down.
today.time_sinks: The call itself is most of the 124 hours. Cheques barely exist here; the hard cases are short payments, SEPA reversals (storno), and damage or detention invoices.

lenses.faster: The call starts with the open items, the last promises, and a plan that already fits the controller's rules. The recap is drafted when the call ends.
lenses.autonomous: A broken promise puts the account on the day's list on its own. The negotiation and the agreement stay with the officer.
lenses.ambitious: Every viable debtor would have a written plan with the cash week and the provision effect visible, and old damage claims would have an owner and an outcome.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the balance from five screens before a call can go. The conversation and a clear agreement are the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Three plans: pay in full with a short grace, instalments inside the officer's mandate, or offset a credit note. Each shows the cash week and any provision.
lenses.altitude: The officer sets the plan rules with the controller: maximum term, minimum first payment, and the point where chasing stops and the file moves on.
reach: The controller's support schedule for the doubtful-debt provision at close.
A commercial-credit note for the finance director when a shipper wants longer terms.
A settled position on damage invoices that operations and finance both touch.

tasks.human_edge: Trust on the call, and the read on whether a plan will be kept by a shipper who will also book next week's loads. That agreement binds the company only when a person makes it.
tasks.pattern_why: The result is an agreement the officer makes with the customer. A model can prepare the numbers, the options, and the recap. The negotiation stays with the person.

in_practice.trigger: A broken promise, an unanswered last reminder, a SEPA reversal, or an open damage invoice reaches the day's list.
steps: Open a brief with the balance, the promises, the disputes, and any loads booked this week.
Show two or three plans inside the controller's rules, with the cash effect of each.
The officer calls and agrees the outcome.
Draft the recap for the officer to send, and write the plan on the debtor.
Route a write-off, a provision, or a cargo hold to the controller.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer conducts the call and sends the recap. The controller approves any plan beyond the officer's mandate and any amount to be written off or provided.
data_needed: Open items, promise history, and dispute codes.
The officer's mandate and the controller's plan rules.
Booked loads at the three sites for that customer.
Linked credit notes and damage invoices.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS dossier, the recap in the mailbox, and the controller's approval on any plan outside the mandate.

evidence.claim: Collections products such as Onguard store payment arrangements and promise dates against open items.
A copilot can assemble the open items and draft a recap mail; the agreement itself has no reliable full automation in a relationship-driven B2B ledger.
AFAS can hold debtor notes and open items for a plan, but instalment schedules may still be kept beside the ledger.

risks: A plan agreed on the phone and never written down is invisible to the cash forecast and the provision.
Offering to release goods held in the warehouse, without operations and without a signed plan, gives away the leverage.
A drafted recap can concede a damage claim the claims process has not accepted.
Pressure wording in a script can breach the company's practice and weaken a later legal file.
research_questions: How many payment plans are agreed in a month, and what share is paid as agreed?
What amount can the officer agree alone, and what must the controller sign?
Which damage invoices are collectable, and which are still inside the claims workflow?
Can AFAS carry an instalment schedule on a debtor, or do plans live in Excel today?

tasks.short: Book incoming payments against the right customer invoices.

today.trigger: Rabobank statement lines have arrived and customers are claiming they have paid.
steps: Open the statement imported into AFAS.
Match lines that quote an invoice number or a betalingskenmerk.
Split lump-sum payments across open invoices by hand.
Mail the customer when the description is too thin to allocate.
Post the clear lines, or hand them to an AR bookkeeper when the officer has no posting rights.
drudgery: Ticking lines that already contain the invoice number.
Splitting a weekly lump sum with no remittance advice.
Answering 'we have paid' while the line sits unmatched.
today.time_sinks: The 123 hours sit on the remainder: lump sums, short payments, and lines with a useless description. Straight matches are tedious when the rules are weak.

lenses.faster: Lines with a known IBAN, amount, and invoice reference clear themselves. The morning's work becomes the unmatched remainder.
lenses.autonomous: When the Rabobank statement arrives, AFAS applies the match rules and clears the open items that pass. Only lines under the threshold are queued.
lenses.ambitious: Every payment would be allocated on the day the statement arrives, so days sales outstanding and the cash forecast do not wait on a person, and the 'already paid' mails dry up.
lenses.joy: Ticking obvious matches off a statement can go. A lump sum the customer nets against a damage credit still needs a short human look.
lenses.options: For an ambiguous lump sum, five allocations against open items, each with the residual and the invoices left open.
lenses.altitude: The officer owns the match rules: IBAN map, reference patterns, and tolerances, and reviews the unmatched ageing with the bookkeepers.
reach: The AR bookkeepers' daily cash application.
The controller's unallocated-cash figure at month close.
Fewer payment-status questions back into the collections mailbox.

tasks.human_edge: The officer recognises a short payment that is a known tariff dispute, and a customer who nets a damage credit without saying so in the description.
tasks.pattern_why: A clear SEPA line is an IBAN, an amount, and a reference, matched to an open item. The result is checkable: the open item clears or it does not. Messy descriptions stay on the exception queue.

in_practice.trigger: The Rabobank statement file is available for import into AFAS.
steps: Import the statement into AFAS.
Match on IBAN, amount, invoice number, and betalingskenmerk.
Post the matches that clear an open item inside the agreed tolerance.
Propose allocations for lump sums and short payments.
Leave the unmatched lines on the shared bookkeeper and officer queue.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer or an AR bookkeeper posts anything below the match threshold. The controller's review of the bank reconciliation at close stays as it is.
data_needed: CAMT.053 or the statement format AFAS already imports from Rabobank.
Debtor IBANs and open items.
The tolerance and the write-off rule for small residuals.
Who is allowed to post on debiteuren.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS bank journal and the match log, including who posted each exception.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit imports bank statements and matches them to open debtor items.
Rabobank business banking provides statement files that accounting systems import.
HighRadius sells cash application that matches remittances to open invoices and queues the remainder.

risks: A wrong match clears the wrong invoice and hides a real overdue balance.
A wide tolerance writes off structural short payments a few euros at a time.
Posting into a closed period during the month close disturbs the ledger the accountant has already tied out.
Bank details in a side Excel file sit outside the AFAS audit trail.
research_questions: What percentage of Rabobank lines auto-match in AFAS today, and how many lines a day are left?
Do customers pay per invoice with a betalingskenmerk, or in weekly lumps?
Who is allowed to post to debiteuren: the officer, the bookkeepers, or both?
Is there a tolerance and a second-person rule for residuals that are written off?

tasks.short: Change customer details and deal with debtors that have closed or died.

today.trigger: A customer asks to change an address, a billing email, or a bank account, or a letter comes back, or a bankruptcy notice arrives.
steps: Read the mail and find the debtor in AFAS.
Check the KvK number when it is on the debtor.
Type the new address, email, or bank account.
Ask the controller what to do with the balance when a company is bankrupt, dissolved, or the sole trader has died.
Leave the history in the dossier because nobody is sure what may be removed.
drudgery: Retyping an address from a mail signature into the debtor card.
Working out which of several branch debtors the request refers to.
Keeping a side note of changes because the reason is not in the audit view people use.
today.time_sinks: The 71 hours are spread thinly: each change is small, but an IBAN change needs a careful check, and a bankruptcy needs the controller. US-style 'purge the deceased' does not fit a Dutch ledger.

lenses.faster: A change mail becomes a filled proposal on the right AFAS debtor, with the source attached, so the officer stops retyping and stops guessing the branch.
lenses.autonomous: A filed request can open a proposal on its own. Saving it, and any change to a bank account, waits for a person. A bankruptcy mark can raise a task when someone checks the KvK status.
lenses.ambitious: Billing master data would stay current for every active debtor, and a bankruptcy or a dissolution would be seen while the balance is still collectable.
lenses.joy: Retyping addresses from signatures can go. Calling a known contact to confirm a new IBAN is the check people want to keep.
lenses.options: When the request is fuzzy, the candidate debtors side by side, with city, KvK number, and open balance, so the wrong branch is not updated.
lenses.altitude: The officer sets the master-data rules with the controller: which fields an email may change, which need a callback, and how a closed debtor is marked and kept.
reach: The AR bookkeepers' debtor-card maintenance.
Fewer invoice failures for whoever sends the bills.
A current contact for the accountant when a credit note must go to a curator.

tasks.human_edge: Confirming a bank-detail change with a known person by phone, and deciding what a bankruptcy or a death means for the open balance and the estate or the curator.
tasks.pattern_why: The input is usually a free-text mail, and the output changes master data. An IBAN change is a fraud risk, and fiscal retention blocks deletion, so a person approves every save.

in_practice.trigger: A mail asks for a master-data change, a letter or reminder bounces, or a bankruptcy or death notice arrives.
steps: Match the request to one AFAS debtor using name, city, and KvK number.
Propose the new field values with the source mail attached.
For an IBAN change, require a callback to a known contact before the proposal can be saved.
For bankruptcy, dissolution, or death, mark the debtor and open a task for the balance.
Keep the invoice history for the fiscal retention period and log who approved the change.
in_practice.human_gate: A person approves every master-data change. An IBAN change also needs the callback. Deletion inside the seven-year retention period is not an allowed outcome.
data_needed: Current debtor master data and KvK number.
The source mail and the known callback contact.
Open balance and legal status.
The fiscal retention rule the accountant follows.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS audit trail on the debtor, with the approver and the source mail.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores debtor master data, including address and bank account, with an audit trail of changes.
Dutch fiscal administration must be kept for seven years, so debtor invoice history is not deleted when a contact dies or a company is dissolved.
Invoice fraud through a mailed IBAN change is a known pattern, and a callback to a known contact is standard treasury practice.

risks: Changing an IBAN from an email alone is a common invoice-fraud route.
Deleting or anonymising invoice history inside the seven-year bewaarplicht conflicts with tax law.
A deceased sole trader's data still needs an AVG basis and a careful handover to the estate.
Three sites can mean three debtor cards for one customer; the wrong card is easy to update.
research_questions: How many debtor master changes happen in a month, and how many of them are IBAN changes?
Does AFAS block deletion of debtors that have open items or historical invoices?
Is the KvK number stored and used, or is the address free text?
What is the written rule for a callback before a bank account is changed?

tasks.short: Stop work for non-payers and hand the file to a lawyer.

today.trigger: The last reminder has expired, the customer has gone quiet, and the balance is above the amount the controller cares about.
steps: Confirm the reminders, the open balance, and that no dispute is recorded.
Tell the controller and ask sales what they know about the customer.
Mail Rotterdam, Tilburg, or Venlo in free text to stop new work or hold goods.
Collect invoices, reminders, the contract, and proofs of delivery into a file.
Send the file to the external lawyer or the incasso bureau.
drudgery: Hunting PDFs across AFAS, Outlook, and SharePoint for a complete file.
Writing a different hold note for each site.
Discovering later that goods were released because the site mail was missed.
today.time_sinks: Assembling the file is most of the 60 hours. The decision is rarer. There is no separate credit department; this officer, the controller, and the finance director are the credit line. Repossession in the retail sense does not apply; the lever is a credit hold and, where the conditions allow, retention of goods already in the warehouse.

lenses.faster: The handover file and the site hold note are assembled from AFAS and SharePoint, with loads already booked named, so the officer stops hunting for PDFs.
lenses.autonomous: When a debtor passes the last policy step, with no dispute and a balance above the floor, a draft hold and a draft handover appear in the controller's queue. Nothing is sent until a person releases it.
lenses.ambitious: Every account that should be on hold would be on hold at all three sites the same day, and the company would see which customers should never have been given those terms.
lenses.joy: Collating PDFs for the lawyer can go. The decision to hold a customer's goods, and the conversation with operations, is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Three next steps side by side: one more call, a credit hold with the booked loads named, or a legal handover. Each shows balance, age, dispute flag, and the site impact.
lenses.altitude: The officer maintains the escalation policy: days, amounts, who signs a hold, who signs a legal file, and how a hold is lifted after payment.
reach: The finance director's rush job of sending a file to external counsel.
The FP&A move of cash from 'expected' to 'doubtful'.
The controller's provision discussion at close.

tasks.human_edge: The decision to hold freight or to sue a customer the commercial team still wants, and the authority to accept the operational damage of that hold.
tasks.pattern_why: The file is a set of lookups and rules. A hold can stop a warehouse, and a legal handover has a cost and an AVG side, so both count only after a person approves them.

in_practice.trigger: A debtor has passed the last reminder step, the balance is above the floor, and no dispute is open.
steps: Assemble invoices, the reminder log, the contract, the proofs of delivery, and the correspondence.
Draft the credit-hold note per site, including loads already booked.
Draft the handover note for the external lawyer or the incasso bureau.
After approval, send the hold to the named site contacts and release the file.
When payment lands, send the lift of the hold and confirm the site has released the block.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller or the finance director approves each credit hold and each legal handover. Operations confirms that the hold is actually in place.
data_needed: The full reminder history and the dispute flag.
The signed warehouse or transport conditions on retention of goods.
Booked loads by site.
The lawyer's or bureau's intake list and the processing agreement.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS dossier and a hold log shared with the sites, including the lift of each hold.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit and SharePoint already store the invoices, reminders, and contract templates a handover file is built from.
Onguard supports escalation steps and handover of a debtor file after internal collection fails.
An automated refusal of further service to a sole trader needs a human decision, and a file sent to a lawyer needs a processing agreement under the AVG.

risks: A hold sent to a site can stop freight the company has no contractual right to retain.
A legal file sent without a processing agreement, or to the wrong external party, is an AVG breach.
Escalating an invoice that is still disputed weakens the claim and the customer relationship.
A hold that is never lifted after payment keeps blocking a site that has already moved on.
research_questions: How many accounts a year are handed to a lawyer or an incassobureau, and how many credit holds are issued?
Is the right to retain goods written into the conditions the customer signed?
Who at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo must receive a hold, and how is the lift confirmed today?
Does the last reminder meet the requirements the company's lawyer wants before accepting a file?

role.altitude: The credit and collections officer becomes the owner of the order-to-cash chase: the rules for terms, reminders, holds, and handover; the quality of debtor data; and the cash-in figure the month-close forecast uses. The ledger, the standard reminders, and the clear bank matches run as a system the officer checks.
reach: The AR bookkeepers' unmatched payments and debtor master changes.
The controller's doubtful-debt support and the monthly explanation of days sales outstanding.
The FP&A analysts' weekly cash-in line in the forecast.
A first credit look before sales confirms terms for a new shipper.
The accountant's pack for a credit note or a write-off that comes out of a collection agreement.
role.ceiling_note: This is one person at a loaded EUR 45 an hour. These eight tasks are about 930 hours a year. Calls, real disputes, payment plans, and the decision to hold freight or to sue do not shrink below the number of live cases. The close still depends on the bookkeepers' bank reconciliation and on operations for proofs of delivery. Customer trust limits how hard a standard reminder can push a shipper the company wants to keep.
skills_to_grow: Write the collection policy as rules the controller can approve: stages, grace days, dispute codes, and the amount the officer may agree.
Test AFAS dunning and bank-match rules and read the match log.
Explain a cash-in week and a doubtful-debt provision in the form FP&A and the controller use at close.
Apply the seven-year fiscal retention and the AVG basics when a file goes to a lawyer or a bureau.
Judge a promise, a plan, and a hold for a shipper with loads booked at the three sites.
role.ambitious_version: Noordhaven would see every open item with a status, a next step, and a cash week, and the forecast at close would already contain what is expected to be paid. Straight SEPA payments would clear on the day of the statement. Standard reminders would go out under a policy the officer maintains, in the right language, with a cost line the contract allows. The officer's day would be broken promises, real damage and detention disputes, and the few holds and legal files, each with a decision the controller can stand behind.
